posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
So I have a dislike of jargon that makes communication inaccessible to people who are inexperienced in the relevant area. It makes a barrier that new people have to work hard to overcome in order to be able to become properly involved in an activity, and definitely risks alienating and discouraging people who might then give up on something they'd ultimately enjoy a lot.

(It's important to note here that as a musician and a scientist, I know that technical terms are necessary and important and we shoouldn't discourage their use, but if you're wanting to explain something to a non-scientist or non-musician you have to think about the words you choose. I wouldn't use "ATP" or "adenosine triphosphate" with someone who hasn't studied biology (I'd say something about "cell energy" maybe) because they wouldn't understand and would perhaps switch off.)

And the point I'm making is, we all use abbreviations on here far more than I think we should. Sure, a lot of forumites are extremely knowledgable about the game and the card names/effects, but there are definitely some people out there who think, "WTM? WTF?" and it concerns me that this kind of thing makes us incomprehensible to the new people that we should be encouraging - more SotM obsessives is better, right?

Disclosure: I have a medical condition (fibromyalgia) which causes me cognitive difficulties - imagine being really tired a lot of the time and finding it difficult to think, kind of like you'd feel if you had proper 'flu and someone asked you to solve even relatively easy algebra questions when you're finding it hard to even keep your eyes open. And personally, even with my greater-than-average familiarity with and knowledge of the cards, I often have trouble knowing what people are talking about just because they've made up some cute nickname or are using initial letters or something. An fairly obvious name, like Akash or Gloomy or Grandpa Legacy or similar would definitely be preferable.

Now I'm not telling people what to do or trying to impose my will on the forum or anything, just asking that people think about it a little, and consider typing a few more letters to confuse new people a bit less (and make my life a bit easier as well).

A completely irrelevant example here, but it illustrates the difficulty I have. I once (for no particular reason other than boredom) found myself on a forum for people who are trying to conceive a child. These places are chock-full of acronyms and infantilisms and it's almost like every third word is in a foreign language. It took me ages to work out what the hell they were talking about, and really I only stayed there as long as I did because I was determined to "beat" the language problems. Here's a few I remember, which are so unintuitive as to be completely unintelligable.

AF = Aunt Flo = menstrual period

BFZ = Big Fat Zero = negative pregnancy test result

BFP = Big Fat Positive = positive preganancy test result

BD = Baby Dust = "good luck in conceiving" wishes

TTC = Trying to conceive

So you get things like, "Me and DH have been TTC for 4 months and keep getting BFNs. Then AF was 2 days late and then a BFP! So excited! Thanks for the BD everyone, here's hoping it's DD2!"

And a good proportion of the threads started with someone saying, "what on earth does AF mean"?

You've probably heard it - the hen finds an ear of wheat and asks the other animals to help her sow, weed, harvest, thresh, grind and bake the wheat into bread. The animals refuse, but all are willing to help eat the loaf. The hen declines to share, and instead she and her chicks eat it. Capitalist propaganda, but there you go. Personally I'd share with animals who were genuinely unable to help rather than just unwilling.

But there's another verion of the story where the hen is forced to share her bread with the animals that didn't want to make effort for it. And as a result, she stops working too - why should she work her butt off just to get the majority of it taken away, leaving her with a few crumbs?

You know that old story about the Americans and the Russians needing a writing implement that would work in low/zero gravity in space? (It's an urban legend, apparently.) The Americans spent a lot of time and money doing research and created a special pen that worked upside down and in zero gravity. The Russians used a pencil.

The pencil here is a few more keystrokes and a little more effort.

I own a Zero Gravity pen that writes upside down, got it at the Science center.

Not that it has anything to do with that particular tale, but I like my fancy pen.

The old saying "you have to have money to make money" is often very meaningful.  "Getting up off your arse" doesn't magically solve all your problems; no amount of effort will accomplish a futile task.  But I wasn't advocating "sitting around waiting for the resourceful to hand out", so much as "getting together into a united front and FORCING the resourceful to hand out".  Not a military solution, mind, but more like a massive act of passive resistance.  I want to see millions of people stop scrabbling for scraps in our plutocratic society, and start making it not a plutocracy anymore.  Refusing to work for pennies, refusing to sit quietly and tolerate government corruption and corporate takeover - I want to see something like the creation of unions to force concessions from management, but on a nationwide scale if not a global one.

The problem is when you apply that thinking in situations where you don't need to fight to get fair treatment.

It is also easy to fall into the trap of viewing yourself as powerless and others as powerful.  Everyone can make a difference, in fact it is often the least powerful who make the greatest differences.  The rich and powerful throw money at problems, but it is up to others to see that money = progress, not by yelling and campaigning, but by being the hands that do the work.  One of the reasons we are in the boat we are in nationally is because we have become a nation of people willing to let those in power solve our problems for us

In this forums you have created (unwittingly or not) an impression that you want us all to do things your way, and don't really give a hoot about what anyone else wants.  That may be a false impression but it exists.  If that is not the impression you are trying to give, then you might want to start actively changing it..

Silverleaf:

So you want the world to magically give you everything you want without you having to actually do anything?

Not just me, I want this for everyone, or at least everyone who wants it.  Other than that, pretty much yes.  To my way of thinking, life is an inconvenience compared to nonexistence, and inherently undesireable unless it is entirely spent enjoying ourselves.  I take games with extreme seriousness, as you've probably noticed, because to me they are little short of a sacrament - every moment we live without being happily preoccupied, we would have been better off not existing, and thus games and similar entertainments justify our lives.  I don't believe we need to earn happiness, I don't believe we have some higher purpose which is worth making sacrifices for, and I don't believe people have the right to succeed at other people's expense, even if the alternative is that nobody ever succeeds at all.  I would be quite satisfied with the entire world agreeing to maintain a happy medium, with everyone just sort of basically content in a very small way.  Injustices of any variety instantly distemper me, so I would single-handedly cure them if I possessed the power to, and lacking that power, I'd rather never hear of their existences.  When I am the "victim" of them, the latter is obviously impossible, and so my only strategy to date has been to b***h at the top of my lungs about it, hoping someone else might be motivated to fix the problem for me, so I can go back to my comfortable little rut without further interruption.
